title: Synthetic populations, state transfer, and modelled publics
selection_rule: Apply the same predicates and evidentiary burdens to the complete or declared comparator universe regardless of party, ideology, nationality, affiliation, investor identity, founder biography, customer identity, or anticipated news value. A target may route discovery but cannot define membership.

cases.title: No. 10 and pandemic-data personnel diaspora
cases.public_interest_question: Which people holding bounded data, digital, research, testing, behavioural, communications, or crisis-response roles in No. 10 and central pandemic machinery later entered private AI, data, consulting, investment, advisory, or governance roles, under one role-neutral battery?
cases.selection_unit: one person named in an official appointment, inquiry artifact, programme record, departmental organogram, honours record, business-appointment decision, company filing, or employer biography
cases.selection_universe: the complete recoverable cohort from declared No. 10, Cabinet Office, DHSC, Covid Inquiry, 10DS, testing-programme, and central crisis-response source families for the frozen 2019-2022 window, before post-government destinations are queried
source_families: Cabinet Office, No. 10 and DHSC records
ACOBA and Civil Service Commission decisions
Companies House and employer leadership pages
forbidden_inferences: same institution proves contact or coordination
cases.acceptance: A reproducible cohort manifest, dated transition ledger, destination taxonomy, coverage report, and matched-comparator analysis in which every role is source-addressable and every unknown remains explicit.

cases.title: 10DS to i.AI to GDS/DSIT institutional succession
cases.public_interest_question: How did experimental data-science and AI units inside No. 10 and the Cabinet Office become, merge into, or transfer functions to later central-government AI and digital institutions?
cases.selection_unit: one formally named unit, programme, mandate, budget line, senior appointment, published strategy, machinery-of-government transfer, or official service
cases.selection_universe: all central UK government units and programmes recoverable from official records whose declared remit included data science, AI incubation, responsible AI, digital centre-of-government work, or cross-government AI implementation from 2019 onward
source_families: Contracts Finder and Find a Tender
forbidden_inferences: absence of transfer notice proves no continuity
cases.acceptance: A time-indexed institutional genealogy with separately evidenced mandate, personnel, programme, budget, and supplier continuity, plus a refusal ledger for apparent but unproved successions.

cases.title: Faculty to Accenture public-sector AI scaling
cases.public_interest_question: What public-sector, campaign, health, defence, and enterprise capabilities, personnel, products, contracts, and governance obligations moved when Accenture acquired Faculty?
cases.selection_unit: one filed acquisition event, named product, employee cohort, director or executive transition, disclosed contract, public-sector framework, customer case, intellectual-property statement, or post-acquisition service
cases.selection_universe: all Faculty legal entities, named products, directors, publicly disclosed customers and contracts, and Accenture units explicitly connected to the transaction, frozen before evaluating political significance
source_families: UK procurement portals and departmental spending
CMA or other competition records if applicable
forbidden_inferences: reported transaction value proves consideration paid
cases.acceptance: A transaction-centred capability ledger showing what demonstrably moved, what remained separate, what was merely marketed as continuity, and which public contracts or programmes changed legal counterparty.

cases.title: Commercialisation of pandemic decision infrastructure
cases.public_interest_question: Which population-response, testing, forecasting, dashboard, behavioural, logistics, and executive-decision capabilities developed or deployed during the pandemic later became commercial products, consultancies, investment theses, or reusable government services?
cases.selection_unit: one named pandemic programme, tool, dataset, contractor deliverable, public official, product launch, company formation, acquisition, patent, funding round, or later customer deployment
cases.selection_universe: all capabilities and suppliers enumerated from a frozen set of official UK pandemic programme, inquiry, NAO, spending, and contract sources, followed forward without selecting only famous founders
forbidden_inferences: pandemic role proves access to reusable personal data
no public successor means no commercialisation
cases.acceptance: A source-complete capability denominator and forward lineage matrix with verified positives, explicit nulls, identity holds, and no causal claim beyond documented transfer or later reuse.

cases.title: Validator-to-adviser scientific legitimacy market
cases.public_interest_question: How do synthetic-population and adjacent AI vendors use academics and researchers as validators, advisers, chief scientists, co-authors, directors, investors, or public credibility carriers, and what independence is actually disclosed at the time of each claim?
cases.selection_unit: one public validation claim, evaluator, advisory appointment, scientific title, consultancy, corporate directorship, publication, grant, compensation disclosure, or replication
cases.selection_universe: the complete recoverable vendor cohort from the frozen Gartner synthetic-population category plus matched adjacent vendors, with every public validation claim and named evaluator captured before role overlap is assessed
source_families: preprints, repositories, supplements, and conference records
forbidden_inferences: later role retroactively changes earlier status
cases.acceptance: A claim-by-claim validation ledger with evaluator role at the relevant date, protocol control, compensation state where public, reproducibility status, and matched-vendor comparison.

cases.title: Centre for Human Progress behavioural-science bridge
cases.classification: nonprofit/company governance and behavioural-science translation case
cases.public_interest_question: What programmes, funding, research, public-policy activity, commercial relationships, and personnel surfaces connect the Centre for Human Progress to behavioural science, cultural evolution, AI, philanthropy, government, and private decision tools?
cases.selection_unit: one filed corporate event, director appointment, programme, publication, grant, donor disclosure, partnership, event, consultancy, company role, or public-policy output
cases.selection_universe: the Centre for Human Progress legal entity, all filed directors and persons of control if any, every publicly named programme and partner, and matched behavioural-science institutes selected under the same organisational predicates
cases.acceptance: A governance-first institutional dossier with a complete public programme and funding inventory, matched comparator, and explicit separation of co-directorship from any receipted transaction.

cases.title: Former-official AI advisory portfolios and post-office controls
cases.classification: post-public-service portfolio and regulatory-control cohort case
cases.public_interest_question: How do former senior officials assemble portfolios of AI, technology, consulting, investment, ethics, and public-private roles, and how effectively do business-appointment controls describe, limit, monitor, and enforce those roles?
cases.selection_unit: one former senior official, approved or disclosed appointment, client or employer, restriction, recusal, lobbying contact, bid participation, board role, compensation state, enforcement event, or expiry date
cases.selection_universe: all former Cabinet Secretaries, permanent secretaries, senior No. 10 officials, and other declared comparator offices leaving within a frozen period, not only Simon Case or AI-linked appointees
source_families: ACOBA and Civil Service Commission decisions
forbidden_inferences: former office proves access was used
multiple roles prove an influence network
cases.acceptance: A complete office-defined cohort, appointment and restriction ledger, restriction-window activity screen, and regulator-effectiveness comparison that preserves both breaches and clean controls.

cases.title: Gartner and analyst-made synthetic-population category
cases.public_interest_question: How did analysts define synthetic population and behavioural simulation as a procurement category, which vendors were selected or excluded, what dimensions and tiers were used, and how did vendors convert paywalled analyst material into public legitimacy?
cases.selection_unit: one analyst report, vendor reviewed, tier assignment, inclusion criterion, quoted analyst statement, licensed excerpt, vendor reproduction, customer procurement reference, or subsequent category change
cases.selection_universe: the complete 60-company reviewed universe and 33-company watched universe reported for Gartner document 7718657, plus any later or predecessor category reports recovered under the same document family
source_families: Gartner document metadata and licensed access
other analyst reports and category taxonomies
forbidden_inferences: vendor quote equals full report context
cases.acceptance: A frozen category denominator, report-method ledger, vendor-claim crosswalk, and category-diff history with every unrecovered portion visibly bounded.

cases.title: Publisher synthetic-audience deployment corpus
cases.public_interest_question: Which publishers and media companies deploy synthetic audiences or simulated readers, what data and lawful roles support them, which editorial, product, marketing, commercial, and advertiser decisions use them, and whether human research continues alongside the models?
cases.selection_unit: one publisher, named product, vendor deployment, dataset class, privacy statement, internal use, advertiser offering, validation claim, procurement record, or documented decision
cases.selection_universe: all publisher and media deployments recovered from the frozen synthetic-population vendor cohort, reciprocal publisher announcements, industry reporting, and procurement sources, including displayed logos held as unresolved until confirmed
cases.acceptance: A source-complete publisher deployment table and claim-granular dossiers that distinguish vendor, customer, policy, regulator, and independent evidence.

cases.title: Modelled populations replacing observed consultation
cases.public_interest_question: Where do synthetic populations, digital twins, virtual personas, agent panels, or simulated stakeholders supplement or replace surveys, interviews, focus groups, citizen consultation, user research, deliberation, or other direct human input?
cases.selection_unit: one documented workflow, decision, consultation, procurement, policy, product feature, evaluation, disclosure, or affected stakeholder process
cases.selection_universe: all named deployments and use cases in the frozen vendor cohort plus source-complete public procurement and case-study records, classified before evaluating whether replacement occurred
source_families: vendor case studies and product documentation
forbidden_inferences: use in one workflow proves organisation-wide substitution
cases.acceptance: A workflow-level substitution ledger with explicit classification thresholds, affected populations, decision stakes, disclosure, appeal routes, and matched controls.

cases.title: Political persuasion and message-optimisation use
cases.classification: political, advocacy, and public-affairs deployment corpus
cases.public_interest_question: Which campaigns, parties, governments, advocacy organisations, lobbying firms, public-affairs consultancies, and issue groups use synthetic audiences or population simulation for message testing, persuasion, mobilisation, fundraising, policy framing, or opposition research?
cases.selection_unit: one disclosed client, contract, campaign filing, consultancy service, product use, case study, ad test, public statement, procurement record, or acceptable-use decision
cases.selection_universe: all political and public-affairs use recovered from the complete vendor cohort and declared official filing systems, with client identity held unresolved until a source supports it
forbidden_inferences: political client proves manipulation or illegality
vendor silence proves hidden political work
cases.acceptance: A legal-name-resolved political-use corpus with capability, sale, contract, expenditure, deployment, prohibition, and null states kept distinct.

cases.title: Government, classified, and defence deployment
cases.classification: public procurement, supplier, and sensitive-environment deployment case
cases.public_interest_question: Which synthetic-population vendors are listed, procured, funded, piloted, subcontracted, or deployed by governments, defence organisations, intelligence-adjacent bodies, emergency services, or classified environments?
cases.selection_unit: one supplier listing, framework lot, opportunity, bid, award, subcontract, grant, pilot, official case study, security claim, department disclosure, or classified-environment capability statement
cases.selection_universe: the complete vendor cohort searched across declared official procurement, grants, supplier-framework, spending, innovation, and company-record sources in each claimed jurisdiction
forbidden_inferences: zero web result proves no government work
cases.acceptance: A reproducible jurisdiction-by-vendor query matrix and award ledger with source-bounded nulls, identity resolution, subcontractor coverage, and no inference beyond the official record.

cases.title: Synthetic-data lineage, consent, and anonymisation
cases.public_interest_question: What personal, panel, survey, behavioural, first-party, public, licensed, inferred, and model-generated data feed synthetic populations, under what lawful and contractual authority, and when do resulting personas or distributions remain personal, re-identifiable, or group-sensitive?
cases.selection_unit: one dataset, data source, controller or processor statement, lawful basis, consent term, licence, retention rule, anonymisation test, re-identification assessment, data-sharing agreement, regulator finding, or deployment
cases.selection_universe: every data source and processing claim disclosed by the frozen vendor and deployment cohort, plus public privacy notices and regulatory records; undisclosed inputs remain gaps rather than inferred data flows
forbidden_inferences: lack of disclosure proves unlawful processing
cases.acceptance: A dataset-to-output lineage graph with legal-role, purpose, retention, rights, and re-identification fields, plus explicit gaps and regulator-standard comparisons.

cases.title: Metric and benchmark governance for synthetic populations
cases.public_interest_question: How are synthetic-population accuracy metrics, benchmarks, holdouts, baselines, subgroup slices, uncertainty, leakage controls, and headline percentages designed, governed, and reproduced across vendors?
cases.selection_unit: one metric definition, benchmark dataset, evaluation question, holdout rule, model version, baseline, subgroup result, error distribution, replication, correction, or marketing claim
cases.selection_universe: every public quantitative validation claim made by the frozen vendor cohort and matched academic methods, captured with page version and date before comparative scoring
source_families: vendor methodology pages and technical papers
forbidden_inferences: proprietary metric is invalid by definition
cases.acceptance: A versioned metric registry, claim ledger, reproducibility classification, baseline comparison, and blind-replication protocol covering the full vendor denominator.

cases.title: Cross-cultural and multilingual extrapolation
cases.public_interest_question: What evidence supports synthetic-population claims across countries, languages, minority groups, political systems, and culturally distinct markets, and where do vendors abstain, localise, or silently extrapolate?
cases.selection_unit: one claimed country, language, population, dataset, validation result, local partner, translation process, cultural adaptation, abstention, deployment, or documented failure
cases.selection_universe: every country and language claimed, evaluated, or deployed across the frozen vendor cohort, compared against the smaller set with public validation evidence
source_families: country-level case studies and customer announcements
forbidden_inferences: one national sample represents all subgroups
cases.acceptance: A country-language coverage matrix separating availability, data support, validation, deployment, localisation, uncertainty, and abstention for every vendor.

cases.title: Foundation-model, cloud, and subprocessor dependence
cases.classification: technical supply-chain, custody, and version-drift case
cases.public_interest_question: Which upstream language models, cloud providers, data platforms, analytics services, security vendors, and subprocessors make synthetic-population products possible, and how do model changes alter validated behaviour, custody, jurisdiction, and customer claims?
cases.selection_unit: one model provider, model version, cloud region, subprocessor, data flow, security certification, contract term, incident, vendor change, validation rerun, or customer deployment
cases.selection_universe: all subprocessors, infrastructure providers, model references, security documents, and technical dependencies publicly disclosed by the frozen vendor cohort, with undisclosed dependencies held as gaps
forbidden_inferences: model change necessarily invalidates all prior results
cases.acceptance: A versioned technical supply-chain map with data custody, model-version, validation-drift, security, and incident fields, including explicit undisclosed dependencies.

cases.title: Capital, board control, and strategic rights
cases.classification: financing, governance, and control-rights cohort case
cases.public_interest_question: Who finances synthetic-population vendors, what securities and governance rights are created, which investors recur across vendors, and how do filed control rights differ from public funding narratives?
cases.selection_unit: one legal entity, funding round, security class, allotment, investor, director or observer appointment, shareholder agreement term where public, PSC state, charge, acquisition, secondary sale, or fund relationship
cases.selection_universe: the complete frozen vendor cohort and every filed financing or ownership event for their legal entities, followed through named funds and individuals without inferring operational influence from investment alone
forbidden_inferences: board seat proves involvement in every decision
cases.acceptance: A filing-first capital and governance ledger with reconciled amounts, rights, actors, recurrence, and explicit separation of economic exposure from documented control.

cases.title: Labour substitution and professional research standards
cases.classification: industry restructuring, workforce, and professional-governance case
cases.public_interest_question: Which market-research, user-research, data, analysis, panel, interviewing, recruitment, and client-service functions are changed or displaced by synthetic populations, and what professional duties continue to govern the work?
cases.selection_unit: one job function, workflow, headcount statement, budget claim, service contract, professional standard, methodology disclosure, client deliverable, redundancy, retraining programme, productivity claim, or quality-control responsibility
cases.selection_universe: all documented deployments and vendor claims concerning speed, volume, headcount, budget, automation, and professional roles across the frozen vendor cohort, plus matched conventional research organisations
source_families: employee, union, regulator, and audit records
forbidden_inferences: job loss proves vendor caused it
synthetic respondent is a human research subject by default
cases.acceptance: A task-level labour and accountability matrix with professional-standard mapping, matched workflows, and strict separation of productivity claims from verified employment effects.

frontier.title: Survey-panel and data-broker supply chain
frontier.research_question: Map panel providers, measurement firms, first-party data holders, brokers, licensors, survey archives, and public datasets that support persona construction, calibration, or validation.
frontier.promotion_condition: A named vendor-to-source disclosure, contract, data-processing record, licence, or reciprocal source.

frontier.title: Synthetic persona likeness, identity, and intellectual-property rights
frontier.research_question: Test whether personas reproduce distinctive real-person, creator, respondent, employee, celebrity, patient, or community attributes and identify consent, publicity, copyright, database, trade-secret, and contractual claims.
frontier.promotion_condition: A named product feature, dispute, licence, policy, or technical demonstration.

frontier.title: Contestability and the right to challenge a modelled public
frontier.research_question: Identify who may inspect, correct, appeal, or override a synthetic representation used in a consequential decision and whether affected groups can contest being represented by it.
frontier.promotion_condition: A named deployment and decision process with identifiable affected stakeholders.

frontier.title: Public consultation and regulatory-impact substitution
frontier.research_question: Search consultations, regulatory impact assessments, policy design, legislative research, public communications, and service design for synthetic-population use.
frontier.promotion_condition: An official procurement, policy document, consultation record, disclosure, or meeting record.

frontier.title: Crisis, emergency, and national-resilience simulation
frontier.research_question: Map use in pandemics, disaster response, civil contingencies, public-order planning, evacuation, supply chains, energy shocks, and national resilience.
frontier.promotion_condition: A named programme, contract, exercise, grant, or official capability statement.

frontier.title: Healthcare, patient, and public-health populations
frontier.research_question: Map synthetic patients, treatment preferences, adherence, health communication, clinical-trial recruitment, public-health messaging, and service planning.
frontier.promotion_condition: A named health deployment, regulated product claim, research protocol, or procurement.

frontier.title: Employment, hiring, and synthetic workforces
frontier.research_question: Test use in hiring, employee sentiment, organisational design, workforce planning, labour negotiations, training, and product testing through simulated employees.
frontier.promotion_condition: A named employer, vendor case, procurement, employment-policy disclosure, or study.

frontier.title: Credit, insurance, pricing, and financial-consumer simulation
frontier.research_question: Search banks, insurers, fintechs, asset managers, credit providers, and regulators for synthetic consumer populations used in product design, pricing, risk, collections, conduct, or stress testing.
frontier.promotion_condition: A named regulated deployment, filing, procurement, audit, or regulator record.

frontier.title: Advertising currencies and measurement governance
frontier.research_question: Trace PAMCo, JICs, audience currencies, clean rooms, customer-data platforms, identity systems, attribution tools, and synthetic personas into advertiser-facing products.
frontier.promotion_condition: A documented data or product integration, contract, standard, or reciprocal customer statement.

frontier.title: Standards, certification, and audit markets
frontier.research_question: Map MRS, ESOMAR, AAPOR, ISO, NIST, IEEE, regulator guidance, private assurance, model audits, and emerging synthetic-data certifications.
frontier.promotion_condition: A published standard, audit scheme, certification, scope statement, or enforcement record.

frontier.title: Patents, trade secrets, and publicly funded intellectual property
frontier.research_question: Search patent families, grants, university spin-outs, public research funding, software repositories, and founder publications for technical lineage.
frontier.promotion_condition: A patent, grant, licence, assignment, spin-out record, or public repository.

frontier.title: Liability, indemnification, and insurance
frontier.research_question: Determine who bears loss when a synthetic population produces misleading, discriminatory, unlawful, or commercially harmful output.
frontier.promotion_condition: Public contract terms, litigation, insurance language, regulator action, or a disclosed incident.

frontier.title: Incident reporting and acceptable-use enforcement
frontier.research_question: Build a corpus of prohibited-use policies, enforcement actions, customer suspensions, safety incidents, disclosed failures, corrections, and model withdrawals.
frontier.promotion_condition: A public incident, enforcement record, customer action, or sufficiently complete policy denominator.

frontier.title: Resellers, consultancies, and white-label deployment
frontier.research_question: Map deployments behind research agencies, consultancies, systems integrators, resellers, advertising platforms, and white-label products.
frontier.promotion_condition: A receipted prime/subcontractor, reseller, integration, procurement, or customer record.

frontier.title: Acquisition, insolvency, and data/model custody
frontier.research_question: Track customer data, persona libraries, validation corpora, prompts, models, contracts, and audit duties when vendors are acquired, fail, restructure, or change control.
frontier.promotion_condition: A filed capital event and publicly addressable custody terms, customer notice, administrator report, or contract.

frontier.title: Public-record retention, FOI, and audit trails
frontier.research_question: Ask whether prompts, persona definitions, outputs, decision logs, model versions, and vendor communications become public records when governments use them.
frontier.promotion_condition: A named public deployment, records schedule, FOI response, audit report, litigation hold, or archival rule.

frontier.title: Group privacy and vulnerable-population representation
frontier.research_question: Test harms remaining after individual anonymisation for small communities, protected classes, children, migrants, patients, political minorities, and geographically concentrated groups.
frontier.promotion_condition: A named dataset, deployment, regulator analysis, impact assessment, complaint, or documented failure.

frontier.title: Election-law classification of synthetic public opinion
frontier.research_question: Determine when synthetic polling, message testing, campaign research, coordinated expenditure, in-kind services, political advertising, or voter modelling triggers disclosure or election rules.
frontier.promotion_condition: A jurisdiction-specific legal source and a named capability, expenditure, contract, or deployment.

frontier.title: Upstream model drift and warranty continuity
frontier.research_question: Test whether warranties, accuracy claims, audits, and customer representations survive model, retrieval, prompt, persona, weighting, or post-processing changes.
frontier.promotion_condition: A versioned change and a claim whose validation or warranty status can be compared before and after.

frontier.title: Synthetic-population market concentration and dependency
frontier.research_question: Measure concentration across vendors, foundation models, clouds, data suppliers, analyst categories, investors, and large customers.
frontier.promotion_condition: A frozen vendor denominator and resolved legal entities plus at least one measurable concentration dimension.

review.promotion_path: candidate packet -> selection gate -> receipt and temporal review -> density and privacy review -> release check
review.cross_case_rule: Compute recurrence only after each case independently establishes its denominator and evidence states.
